Only eight participants in that efficacy comparison had HB, so the subgroup estimate remains imprecise. These within-participant comparisons were not randomized. Thrombotic risk and breakthrough-bleed treatment still need a specialist plan.

evidence.snippet: The most frequent disease-presenting symptoms in hemophilia B (hematomas and oral bleeding) differed from those in FVII deficiency (epistaxis and central nervous system bleeding).

nodes.description: Dental extraction and surgery can uncover mild disease as well as provoke severe bleeding in all activity classes.

evidence.reference_title: Hemophilia B.
evidence.snippet: Hemophilia B is characterized by deficiency in factor IX clotting activity that results in prolonged oozing after injuries, tooth extractions, or surgery, and delayed or recurrent bleeding prior to complete wound healing.

nodes.description: Severe or moderate untreated FIX deficiency usually prolongs aPTT; mild disease may escape this screening test. An inhibitor or other intrinsic-pathway defect can produce the same result, so aPTT alone is not diagnostic.

evidence.reference_title: [Acquired haemophilia B: a case report and literature review].
evidence.snippet: an isolated prolongation of the activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) with a reduced factor IX level

evidence.reference_title: Hemophilia B.
evidence.snippet: The diagnosis of hemophilia B is established in individuals with low factor IX clotting activity.

nodes.description: Regular individualized FIX prophylaxis is recommended for severe disease and for moderate or mild disease with frequent bleeds. Targets should prevent bleeding and allow activity; a trough just above 1% may be inadequate for some people, especially with existing joint disease.

evidence.reference_title: International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis clinical practice guideline for treatment of congenital hemophilia A and B based on the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation methodology.
evidence.snippet: Strong recommendations were issued for prophylactic over episodic treatment for severe and moderately severe hemophilia A and B.

evidence.reference_title: Hemophilia B.
evidence.snippet: For those with severe hemophilia B and those with moderate or mild hemophilia B and frequent bleeding, prophylactic treatment with factor IX concentrate infusions to maintain factor IX clotting activity higher than 1% or as needed to prevent bleeding and allow normal activity improves outcomes and prevents chronic joint disease.

nodes.description: Recombinant FIX-WT and R338L activity, activation, inactivation and FVIIIa dependence were compared in purified-protein and plasma systems, including transgene-expressing patient samples. Emicizumab substitution removed Padua-specific hyperactivity.
nodes.id: Purified and plasma FIX-Padua cofactor-dependence assays

evidence.reference_title: Hyperactivity of factor IX Padua (R338L) depends on factor VIIIa cofactor activity.
evidence.snippet: We observed that the high-specific-activity of FIX-R338L requires factor VIIIa (FVIIIa) cofactor.

nodes.description: Preventive MTX plus EHL-FIX improved synovitis and cartilage outcomes compared with FIX alone. Delayed MTX reduced synovial endpoints but did not improve cartilage erosion or proteoglycan loss.

evidence.reference_title: Targeting synovitis by immunomodulation as a novel therapeutic approach for hemophilic arthropathy.
evidence.snippet: No differences in cartilage erosion and proteoglycan loss were observed.

nodes.description: The defining laboratory abnormality is deficient clotting activity, not necessarily reduced antigen concentration.

evidence.reference_title: Hemophilia B.

nodes.description: Physical therapy evaluates and treats musculoskeletal disease; rehabilitation, exercise adapted to joint status, and pain care accompany bleed prevention. Established arthropathy may require orthopedic treatment and does not necessarily resolve when FIX levels rise.

evidence.reference_title: Hemophilia B.
evidence.snippet: Physical therapy for evaluation and treatment of musculoskeletal disease; standard treatments for pain with help from a pain specialist as needed
